column1: # pieces.tsv — EVERYTHING this repository installs and keeps, one piece per line (docs/8-maintenance/4-this-repository.md,
# "The inventory"). The maintenance agents read it as the list of what to maintain; install/verify.sh enforces it (every
# tracked file of common/, legion/, lib/ and install/ belongs to a piece; each installer is where its "how" says);
# common/agent/audit-void.sh checks on each machine that what its pieces install is there.
# A new piece, or a piece that moves: change this file in the same commit (verify.sh fails otherwise).
# Columns, separated by TABs ("-" = none); one piece per function, as an xbps package (each file has one owner):
#   machines  L (Legion), I (IdeaPad), LI (both): where it is installed (the IdeaPad follows its own recipe in Common)
#   stage     stage of docs/reinstall.md and install/install.sh (1–19); "-" for tools
#   how       root | user   run directly at that stage: in install/install.sh, and in docs/reinstall.md or its page
#             manual        by hand, as its page says (the installer is named in that page)
#             via:<id>      installed by the installer of piece <id> (which names this one's installer)
#             tool          not installed (diagnostics, generators, the repository's own tools)
#   installer the repository path that installs it (a script, or the file the stage copies)
#   sources   repository paths that belong to it (a folder ends in /), space-separated
#   installs  what proves it is installed, space-separated: paths (~ = home; * = pattern; no spaces),
#             grep:<file>:<regex> (a line of that file; for a setting written into a shared file) or
#             xbps-local:<package> (installed from a local repository: our patched build, not Void's). "-" only for a
#             manual setting nothing on disk proves (Steam's own settings)
#   undo      how it is undone, like xbps-remove: --remove (its installer takes it), rm (delete the paths of installs,
#             copies in ~), via (the other piece's undo), a command, or what it is ("base system: not undone")
# How to decide each column (what a piece is, which paths, how to undo, settings made by hand, removing a piece):
